paragraphs: An astonishing story about him is told in the Zohar, Balak 204b: he had died, and Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, went to perform an act of kindness for him; afterwards he lived for twenty-two years.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The death and later twenty-two years of life are part of the Zohar story as Hyman reports it. The act of kindness is not specified as burial rites.

The consulted Zohar Balak narrative names Rabbi Yose of Peki’in and Rabbi Elazar, describes Yose’s death and revival, and says twenty-two years were added to his life. The selected continuation carries folio overlays 205a–205b. Hyman’s 204b locator and expansion to Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon are retained as his report; the selected narrative does not independently establish that patronymic or his edition’s pagination.
